response.passage: Natural disasters like earthquakes, floods, and cyclones require immediate and planned action to ensure survival. During an earthquake, the ground shakes violently, making it dangerous to use elevators or stand in doorways, as these can collapse. Instead, you should drop, cover, and hold on under a sturdy table. After the shaking stops, never light a match or candle to inspect your home, as leaking gas pipes could cause an explosion. Floods are equally deceptive; floodwater is often contaminated with sewage and chemicals, making it unsafe to walk through even if it looks like clear rainwater. Furthermore, floods can occur in your area even if it is not raining locally, due to heavy rainfall upstream. When a cyclone warning is issued, do not rely on social media rumors; follow only official government alerts. Many people mistakenly believe they are safe staying home during a severe cyclone, but if authorities order an evacuation, you must move to a designated shelter immediately to avoid the deadly impact of storm surges, which are far more dangerous than normal high tides. Finally, always keep an emergency kit ready well in advance, because once a disaster begins, you will not have the time or safety to gather essential supplies. A family plan ensures everyone knows where to meet, preventing confusion during the chaos.
response.summary: Natural disasters are unpredictable and dangerous, requiring prior preparation and adherence to official safety protocols. Understanding the specific risks of each disaster helps families stay safe and avoid common mistakes.
